### 1. Scene
A raw snack plate: a whole apple, almonds, cherry/grape tomatoes, red grapes, and spinach.

### 2. Vessel
A shallow dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3. Items
Apple, almonds, tomatoes, red grapes, and spinach leaves. No visible oil, dressing, or sauce.

### 4–7. Area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares represent the visible footprint of each food, without double-counting overlaps. Heights are average pile-envelope heights.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole apple | 10% | 53 × 3.0 = 159 ml | 0.85 g/ml | 135 g | 52 | 70 kcal |
| Almonds | 19% | 101 × 1.2 = 121 ml | 0.55 g/ml | 67 g | 579 | 388 kcal |
| Tomatoes | 12% | 64 × 1.8 = 115 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 75 g | 18 | 14 kcal |
| Red grapes | 8% | 42 × 1.7 = 71 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 46 g | 69 | 32 kcal |
| Spinach | 16% | 85 × 1.6 = 136 ml | 0.13 g/ml | 18 g | 23 | 4 kcal |

**Covered area: 65%**, leaving approximately 35% of the plate exposed.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimated **341 g and 508 kcal** are plausible for one modest apple, a substantial pile of almonds, several tomatoes and grapes, and a small handful of leaves. Almonds provide most of the energy. Overall uncertainty is roughly ±20–25%.
